# An override may be written in a different file of the package from the
# declaration it overrides, and its body resolves against the imports of the
# file it was written in. It was checked against the declaration's file: a body
# is checked with its component's file current, and with the override
# installed that component was the base, so `gen` below was undefined in the
# file that imports it.

sngl check p
stdout 'b.sngl: ok'

-- p/a.sngl --
import build "sngl:build"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component block build.family

component text(full string) block

component bar(blocks ...component block) root

component badge(label string) ui.node {
    ui.text(value=label)
}
-- p/b.sngl --
import gen "sngl:x/gen"
import go "sngl:language/go"
import ui "sngl:ui"

func enc(xs list<string>) => xs.join(",")

component block[go.language] {
    gen.emit(render=enc)
}

component text[go.language] {
    gen.node(value=full)
}

// The same for an override of an ordinary component.
component badge[go.language] {
    ui.text(value="[" + label + "]")
}
